# wrnty — full context

> Track every warranty and receipt, get reminded before they expire, and export a claim-ready PDF — one-time purchase, no subscription.

wrnty is an iOS app for iPhone and iPad that keeps product warranties and receipts organised, reminds you before each warranty expires, and lets you export a PDF pack for insurance and warranty claims. It is built by 12F ApS, a small studio in Denmark, and is designed to be private by default: there is no account, nothing is uploaded to the developer, and your data stays on your device (syncing only through your own iCloud if you enable it).

## Why it exists

Most people lose money not because a product fails, but because it fails just after the warranty lapsed — and they never knew the date, or couldn't find the receipt. wrnty fixes both problems: it remembers the expiry date and reminds you before it passes, and it keeps the receipt, serial number and photos attached to each item so a claim is a two-minute job instead of an archaeology dig through a drawer.

## Key Facts

- Platform: iOS (iPhone and iPad, iOS 17 or later)
- Pricing model: free to track up to 2 warranties; Premium is a one-time in-app purchase (no subscription) that removes the item limit and adds expiry alerts, iCloud sync and PDF export
- Privacy: no account required; data stored on-device and in the user's own iCloud; no ads, no tracking, no data selling; optional anonymous analytics that can be turned off; GDPR compliant
- Languages: available in 28 languages
- Developer: 12F ApS, Denmark (https://12f.dk/)
- Website: https://wrnty.12f.dk/
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/wrnty-warranty-receipts/id6747742961

## Features

- Track warranties with product name, brand, merchant, price, purchase and expiry dates, serial number and notes
- Attach receipts and documents as photos and PDFs
- Expiry reminders delivered to the Home and Lock Screen (Premium)
- Home and Lock Screen widgets showing what's expiring next
- Export warranties to PDF for insurance and warranty claims (Premium)
- iCloud sync across iPhone and iPad, plus share & print (Premium)
- Spotlight search to jump straight to a product from iOS search
- Organise by category, brand and purchase date; a running total of the value you have under warranty
- Dark mode and full VoiceOver accessibility

## Who it's for

- People with lots of electronics (phones, laptops, headphones, cameras) whose warranties expire unnoticed
- Homeowners tracking multi-year guarantees on appliances and furniture
- Anyone who buys extended warranties or protection plans and wants to actually use them when something breaks

## Blog

The wrnty blog publishes practical advice on tracking warranties, organising receipts and buying smart at https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/ (RSS feed: https://wrnty.12f.dk/feed.xml). Posts are tagged `warranty-tips`, `organizing` or `buying-guides`.

### What a warranty actually covers on phones, laptops and gadgets (2026-07-31, warranty-tips)
https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/what-your-warranty-actually-covers/
Most people think a warranty covers everything that breaks. It does not. A standard manufacturer warranty covers defects in materials and workmanship — the kind of faults that appear without external damage. Cracked screens, water damage, battery wear, and theft are not included. This post walks through what is and is not covered, explains extended and accidental-damage plans, and shows you how to keep track of what protection you actually have.

### What counts as proof of purchase — and what to do without a receipt (2026-07-31, warranty-tips)
https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/what-counts-as-proof-of-purchase/
A warranty claim usually requires proof of purchase, but the receipt is only one acceptable form. This post covers what companies will and won't accept — bank statements, order confirmations, account records, gift receipts, and more — plus a practical approach to rebuilding your proof when the original receipt is gone, including the one piece of information that unlocks almost every alternative.

### Consumer rights when something breaks — statutory explained (2026-07-31, warranty-tips)
https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/consumer-rights-when-something-breaks/
A manufacturer warranty is one layer of protection, but in many countries you have separate statutory rights against the seller that are not the same thing. This post explains how consumer law and manufacturer warranties differ, when each applies, and how to use both to get a fair outcome when something you bought turns out to be faulty.

### Warranty gotchas — the fine print that voids your cover (2026-07-30, warranty-tips)
https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/warranty-gotchas-fine-print/
Many warranties contain clauses that void coverage under common, everyday conditions — improper use, unauthorised repairs, exposure to moisture, or even opening the device yourself. This post walks through the most common warranty gotchas, how to spot them before you buy, and what to do when you suspect your cover has been invalidated.

### Repair it or replace it? A simple way to decide (2026-07-30, warranty-tips)
https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/repair-it-or-replace-it/
When something breaks, the repair quote often lands in an awkward middle ground — expensive enough to make you hesitate, cheap enough that replacement feels like waste. This post lays out a practical framework for that decision: how to weigh repair cost against replacement value, when a warranty claim should be your first move, and how to factor in the item's age and your actual likelihood of needing it again.

### How to organise receipts so you can actually find them (2026-07-30, organizing)
https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/how-to-organise-receipts/
Keeping receipts doesn't require a filing system or a weekend project. It requires two minutes a day — one minute when you buy something, one minute when you get home. This post walks through a low-friction system that actually works: capture immediately, sort weekly, and know exactly where to look when something breaks.

### How to make a warranty claim (and what to do when it's refused) (2026-07-30, warranty-tips)
https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/how-to-make-a-warranty-claim/
A warranty only pays out if you know how to use it. This post walks through the complete process: proving purchase, contacting the right department, keeping a paper trail, and what to do when they refuse — including escalation paths, your statutory rights, and when it is cheaper to walk away.

### How long is the warranty on common things — a plain reference (2026-07-30, warranty-tips)
https://wrnty.12f.dk/blog/how-long-is-the-warranty-on-common-things/
Most products carry a standard one-year manufacturer warranty, but some categories vary widely — large appliances often two to five years, tyres are covered by tread-wear programs, and mattresses carry anything from two to twenty depending on the brand. This post walks through the most common categories and reminds you that statutory rights against the seller often stack on top of any manufacturer warranty, giving you extra cover in many countries.
